title: Reusable CFG interchange draft
description: Versioned, function-level control-flow graph. Edges describe possible immediate execution transfers, not PDG control, data, or execution dependencies. Structural validation does not prove extraction completeness or semantic correctness.

schema_version.description: CFG interchange version, independent of producer and extraction-profile versions.

profile.description: Versioned construction policy, including granularity, exits, and evaluation-order handling.

producer.description: Frontend identity and settings affecting graph extraction.

name.description: Producer name; a hand-authored example must not claim compiler extraction.

language_version.description: Known language version or explicit missing evidence.

configuration.description: Build flags, frontend options, and other extraction settings. Keys are producer-specific.

sources.description: Source artifacts referenced by spans. Embedded content is optional and useful for self-contained fixtures.

function.description: Identity and source boundary of the single function represented by this graph.

id.description: Opaque function identity, not a clone-matching label.

name.description: Known function name, or a reason it is unavailable.

source_span.description: Function range in its source, using half-open UTF-8 byte offsets.

entry_node_id.description: ID of the unique synthetic entry node. Semantic validation checks that it exists and has no incoming edges.

exit_node_ids.description: IDs of synthetic exit nodes, including distinct normal and exceptional exits when represented. An exit may be unreachable; divergence must not be given a fabricated execution edge to an exit.

nodes.description: Unordered node collection. Each non-boundary node contains one operation or an ordered basic block under the profile. IDs are graph-local.

edges.description: Unordered directed multigraph edges representing immediate possible transfers. Parallel edges preserve distinct branch outcomes; array order has no execution meaning.

extraction_evidence.description: Explicit coverage evidence. A complete claim must be independently checked against the declared profile; an empty edge list is not evidence of no flow.

status.description: Whether all flow required by the profile is represented for this function.

limitations.description: Omitted constructs, conservative approximations, and unavailable facts. Empty only when no limitations are known.

extensions.description: Optional namespaced facts or links to a PDG. These do not change base CFG semantics without a named profile.

id.description: Nonempty opaque identifier; identity is separate from semantic equality.

stringFact.description: A known string or explicit missing evidence; unknown must not be silently treated as an empty value.

value.description: Recorded value; an empty string is a known empty value.

status.description: Why a value is not recorded.

reason.description: Actionable explanation of missing or inapplicable evidence.

span.description: Half-open UTF-8 byte range [start, end). Semantic validation checks source existence and 0 <= start <= end <= source byte length.

source_id.description: ID of the containing source artifact.

start.description: Inclusive byte offset, not a character or line number.

source.description: A source artifact with navigation and stale-span detection evidence.

path.description: Navigation path, not a semantic matching label.

content_identity.description: Algorithm-qualified digest of exact source bytes, or explicit unavailable evidence.

content.description: Optional exact source text. Byte offsets address this string encoded as UTF-8, not JSON escape sequences.

profile.description: Extraction policy identity and essential construction decisions. Referenced policy documents must specify supported constructs; this is not a TinyPDG or CCGraph reproduction claim.

name.description: Name of the independently documented extraction policy.

granularity.description: Operation mode requires one operation per non-boundary node; basic-block mode permits ordered operations with no internal branching.

evaluation_order.description: Machine-checkable policy choices for sequencing and conditional evaluation. Semantic validation must still check the graph against these choices.

exceptional_flow.description: Whether exceptional transfers are explicitly modeled, overapproximated, or excluded. Omissions affecting this function require partial extraction evidence.

exit_policy.description: Normal/exceptional termination, nonreturning calls, and divergence policy. Analysis-only virtual exits must not masquerade as executable edges.

unreachable_code.description: Whether unreachable source operations are retained as disconnected nodes or omitted; reachability is derived from entry.

evaluationOrder.description: Evaluation-order policy, not a claim that source order universally equals execution order. Choices apply to the source language under the versioned extraction profile.

sequencing.description: Preserve language-mandated sequencing. Do not impose a global left-to-right or right-to-left order on constructs whose ordering is not specified by the language. Operations within a basic block remain execution-ordered.

short_circuit.description: explicit_branches splits conditional evaluation into CFG paths so skipped operands are not executed unconditionally. This covers logical short-circuit operators and conditional expressions where applicable. reject requires a diagnostic and non-complete extraction evidence if such a construct is encountered.

unspecified_order.description: overapproximate represents all language-permitted relative evaluation orders without asserting an arbitrary mandatory order; extra paths must be disclosed as approximations. reject requires a diagnostic and non-complete extraction evidence when unspecified or indeterminately sequenced evaluations are encountered. A single chosen order is not a supported policy.

node.description: CFG vertex. A condition node ends in a predicate; transfer nodes end in an abrupt transfer. Source-backed operations carry spans; synthetic boundaries carry origin explanations.

id.description: Graph-local node identity; stable snapshots may sort nodes by ID.

kind.description: Boundary, straight-line operation/block, branching predicate, or abrupt transfer such as return/break/continue/throw.

origin.description: How this node was extracted or synthesized, including frontend/lowering provenance where relevant.

exit_kind.description: Termination category; present only on exit nodes. Divergence is not an exit.

operations.description: Execution-ordered operations, empty on entry/exit nodes. Internal branches must be split into separate nodes.

operation.description: Source-backed operation or predicate. This draft does not supply binding, def/use, alias, or call-effect facts; those are additional inputs to PDG construction.

id.description: Document-local operation identity, usable in a later CFG-to-PDG correspondence.

original_kind.description: Original frontend or language-specific operation kind; not a universal PDG label.

text.description: Human-readable source or display text; not an authoritative semantic label or substitute for binding facts.

source_span.description: Source origin of this operation. Synthetic lowered operations need a future profile extension rather than invented source ranges.

edge.description: Possible immediate control transfer from source to target. Cycles are allowed. A loop back edge is an ordinary transfer with optional loop-role metadata, not a dependence edge.

id.description: Graph-local edge identity, preserving distinct parallel transfers.

kind.description: Transfer kind: normal fallthrough/unconditional flow, predicate outcome, switch outcome, or abrupt transfer. Return edges target a normal exit unless cleanup intervenes.

case_value.description: Case outcome under the profile's serialization policy, present exactly when kind is case.

loop_role.description: Optional loop-structure annotation checked against the extraction policy. Omission means unrecorded, not that the edge is outside a loop.

reason.description: Optional explanation, particularly for conservative exceptional or termination transfers.
